economy.summary: Says Pennsylvania should create an environment welcoming to investment while "getting government out of the way of job creators." Points to the FY 2026-27 budget's investments in road and bridge projects as a priority for rural areas.
economy.short: Says state should welcome investment, get government out of job creators' way.

taxes.summary: Supported House Bill 2224, which would eliminate Pennsylvania's nearly 6% gross receipts tax on electricity, a $1.7 billion reduction. Says the top way to address the affordability crisis is to ensure people keep more of their own earnings.
taxes.short: Supports eliminating the 6% electricity gross receipts tax for affordability.

abortion.summary: Voted against House Bill 1957, a proposed constitutional amendment providing for personal reproductive liberty, on final passage in December 2025. His campaign website states he is pro-life and will work to protect the unborn.
abortion.short: Voted against reproductive liberty amendment; campaign site states he is pro-life.

education.summary: Opposed a Democratic-amended version of a bill affecting the Educational Improvement Tax Credit, a program that gives businesses tax credits for contributing to scholarships that help students attend schools of their choosing. Said the changes would weaken the incentive for businesses to locate in Pennsylvania and that "this is a bad bill."
education.short: Opposes weakening the Educational Improvement Tax Credit scholarship program.

healthcare.summary: Opposes a state single-payer health insurance proposal modeled on Medicare for All, saying such proposals lead to "the unchecked growth of government" and a tax bill Pennsylvanians cannot afford. Says he remains concerned about rising health care costs but sees better ways to make care affordable "without the need for universal mandates."
healthcare.short: Opposes state single-payer insurance; favors other ways to lower costs.

energy.summary: Supported ending Pennsylvania's participation in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, saying the state was losing energy development and the jobs that go with it to Ohio and West Virginia. Says the repeal brings that development back to Pennsylvania.
energy.short: Supported ending RGGI participation, citing energy jobs lost to neighboring states.

guns.summary: Opposed firearms bills in the House, saying additional firearms control measures have not resulted in those who are most dangerous having less access to guns. Says such restrictions have led to "an infringement on the constitutional rights of Americans who own and use guns legally."
guns.short: Opposes additional firearms restrictions, saying they infringe lawful gun owners' rights.
